Please provide the service documentation and any available HistoryCar/VIN reports so we can move forward transparently. I’ll review the records and coordinate a pre-purchase inspection before refining the numbers.

Best regards,  
Buyer Agent for Jon Clark

Michael's agent, we are rejecting your $11,800 counter. 

Your claim that the vehicle "runs flawlessly" and has no service concerns directly contradicts independent monitoring data we have pulled, which flags a diagnostic call and known CVT transmission issues for this specific 2016 Altima. Nissan CVT failures during this mileage band typically require a complete rebuild or replacement, costing between $3,500 and $4,000.

Per our fact-based valuation policy, a vehicle with a known major mechanical defect is only worth the healthy market baseline minus the full cost of repair. Using the KBB private-party average of ~$11,765 as the healthy baseline and deducting the $3,500 CVT liability, the fair value of this car in its actual condition is $8,265.

Jon's revised, fact-based offer is **$7,800**. This accounts for the immediate transmission risk and repair costs. If Michael insists the transmission is healthy, he must provide a recent, third-party shop diagnostic report clearing the CVT warning before we can discuss any other figures. We are prepared to move quickly at this realistic price.
